subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the area of the triangle formed by the straight line x − 4y + 2 = 0 with the coordinate axes.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 4, book p.140. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives the first mark for comparing with ax + by + c = 0 and naming the area formula, and the second for substituting and reaching a positive number. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Answer checked by a second route: the intercepts are x = −2 and y = 1/2, so the area is ½|(−2)(1/2)| = 1/2, which matches the formula result. Related card in the same unit: ts_ipe_m1b_sl_vsaq_area_with_axes asks the same method on 3x − 4y + 12 = 0 and comes from a different source book; the two are separate questions with different numbers, not duplicates.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name the area formula for a line with the two axes, then say what you substitute.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Read off the coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark. The triangle a line cuts from BOTH axes has a formula of its own, Δ = c²/(2|ab|), so nothing has to be set up except the comparison with ax + by + c = 0.
steps.memory_tip: Compare with ax + by + c = 0; the axes-triangle area is c²/(2|ab|).
lines: Compare it with ax + by + c = 0
Area of the triangle is  Δ = c²/(2|ab|)

recall.must_convey: That the line is compared with ax + by + c = 0 to read a = 1, b = −4, c = 2, and the area formula Δ = c²/(2|ab|) is written.

heard_as: a x plus b y plus c

steps.why: The formula already contains both intercepts and the right angle at the origin, so the two intercepts need not be found separately.
common_mistakes: Getting the sign of c wrong after rearranging the equation.

steps.label: Compute the area
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Substitute and simplify. The modulus in the denominator is what keeps the answer positive, and the unit is square units.
steps.memory_tip: An area is never negative — the modulus sign in the denominator is what guarantees that.

lines.text: ∴ Area of the triangle is 1/2 sq.units

steps.why: |ab| = |(1)(−4)| = 4 is positive even though b is negative, so the area comes out positive without any extra sign work.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the 2 in the denominator and writing 4/4 = 1.
